Character Creation

Arneyan Campaign Setting

A quick-reference overview of how a character comes together in Arneyan, with a short summary of each section below. Full detail for each section is given in its own part of this document. Classes are covered in Book III: Classes and aren't repeated here.

Follow these steps in order. Each one points to the section that covers it in full.

Step 1 — Choose an ancestry. Note its size, speed, traits, languages and its fixed attribute bonus and penalty (see Ancestries, below). Choose a subtype if your ancestry has one.

Step 2 — Choose a class and Kit. Read the class's section in Book III: Classes. You gain its 1st-level features and your Kit abilities straight away.

Step 3 — Generate attributes. Use Method V, assign the six scores, then apply your ancestry bonus and penalty and look up each modifier on the compressed table. No attribute can start above 18 (see Starting Scores).

Step 4 — Roll Starting Luck. Roll 4d6, drop the lowest die and add the rest. This is both your Starting Luck and your Current Luck.

Step 5 — Work out hit points. At 1st level, Max HP is the maximum of your class Hit Die plus your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). From 2nd level you roll the die and add your Constitution modifier each level, or take the average. From 11th level you gain a flat amount instead, a third of your Hit Die rounded down (d4 +1, d6 +2, d8 +2, d10 +3, d12 +4), plus your Constitution modifier (minimum 1 HP a level). Each class lists its amount.

Step 6 — Choose skills and languages. You have 3 skill (NWP) slots, each on a different skill. You know your ancestry's languages plus one more for each point of Intelligence modifier, plus any your ancestry lets you choose.

Step 7 — Choose a Feat. Every class gains one at 1st level. Choose from the General Path and the path or paths open to your class.

Step 8 — Choose spells, if you cast. Casters choose their cantrips and spells using their class section and the Spellcasting book.

Step 9 — Buy equipment. Roll your class's starting gold and spend it from the Shopkeeper's Catalogue. Your carrying capacity is 18 slots (20 at Strength 16 or more, 16 at Strength 6 or less).

Step 10 — Choose an alignment and a Background Story. Pick an alignment (see Alignment in Arneyan) and write a few lines on where your character comes from. The Background Story Bonus can later grant Advantage when it applies.

Step 11 — Fill in the numbers. AC = 10 + armour bonus + Dexterity modifier (limited by armour category) + shield + any Feat or class bonuses. Attack roll = d20 + attribute modifier + BtH. Saving throw = d20 + attribute modifier + the greater of 1 and half your level (Fortitude uses Constitution, Reflex uses Dexterity, Will uses Wisdom). Initiative = d20 + Dexterity modifier. Speed comes from your ancestry.

Worked Example: Brenna, Dwarf Fighter

Ancestry: Dwarf — Medium, speed 25ft, darkvision 60ft, +2 Constitution, +1 Wisdom, −1 Charisma.

Class and Kit: Fighter (d10 Hit Die, BtH +0) with the Gladiator Kit. At 1st level she has Weapon Specialisation, Combat Manoeuvres and Combat Reflexes, plus the Kit's Crowd's Favourite and Arena Presence.

Attributes: Method V Set Alpha gives 17, 15, 14, 12, 11, 9. Brenna assigns Strength 17, Constitution 15, Dexterity 14, Wisdom 12, Intelligence 11, Charisma 9. The Dwarf bonuses make Constitution 17, Wisdom 13 and Charisma 8. Her Feat (below) raises Constitution to 18. Modifiers: Strength +2, Dexterity +1, Constitution +3, Intelligence +0, Wisdom +1, Charisma −1.

Luck: She rolls 4d6 and gets 5, 4, 3, 2. Dropping the 2 gives a Starting Luck of 12.

Hit points: Maximum of the d10 (10) plus Constitution modifier +3 = 13, plus 1 from Toughness = 14 Max HP.

Skills and languages: Heraldry, Cooking and Engineering in her 3 NWP slots, plus Armourer as the Dwarf's free Craft skill. Intelligence +0 gives no bonus language, so she knows only her ancestry languages.

Feat: Toughness (+1 Max HP per level, +1 Constitution, Advantage on Constitution checks).

Equipment: She rolls 3d6 for starting gold (4, 5, 3 = 12), so 12 × 10 = 120 gp. She buys a Chain Mail Shirt (100 gp), a Medium Wooden Shield (5 gp), a Spear (1 gp) and a Backpack (2 gp): 108 gp, with 12 gp left. These take 4 of her 20 slots, since the Backpack takes none.

AC: 10 + 4 (Chain Mail Shirt) + 1 (Dexterity; Medium armour allows up to +2) + 1 (shield) = 16.

Attack: With her Spear, d20 + 2 (Strength) + 0 (BtH) = +2, and Advantage on the first attack each round through Weapon Specialisation.

Saves: Fortitude +4 (Constitution +3, plus 1), Reflex +2 (Dexterity +1, plus 1), Will +2 (Wisdom +1, plus 1).

• Size & Traits: sets your size, speed, darkvision, a fixed attribute bonus and penalty, and a handful of innate traits
  • Humanoids: a lore catch-all for generic NPCs only — not a selectable option at character creation

See Arneyan Ancestries — Stats & Mechanics Reference for every ancestry's complete stat block, traits, and attribute modifiers.

• Method V: roll two sets of six descending dice pools (8d6 down to 3d6), then choose one set to keep
  • Safety Nets: the Donation Rule and the Gygaxian Threshold stop anyone ending up with an unplayable character
  • Quick Roll (optional): 4d6, dropping the lowest, six times, with the same threshold and cap
  • Starting Scores: no score starts above 18; ancestry or creation-feat points that would go over move to another attribute
  • Modifiers: attribute modifiers follow Arneyan's compressed scale

See Attributes and Method V for the complete rolling procedure and table rules.

• What It Is: a seventh, fluctuating stat separate from your six attributes — fate's favour and your character's raw survival instinct
  • Starting Score: roll 4d6 drop lowest
  • Burn: +1 per point spent on a d20 roll (attack, save or check; never damage)
  • Luck Checks: roll d20 equal to or under your Luck when fate itself is in question (the only roll-under mechanic)
  • Last Chance: a dying character may burn 1 Luck to make an immediate stabilisation roll (Fortitude save, DC 10); success stops the dying but leaves them unconscious
  • Recovery: +1 on levelling up, plus GM rewards (including +1 for an Alignment Action) — never from rest alone; Luck can never exceed 20

See The Luck Stat for the complete mechanic and the GM's guidance on running it at the table.

• Progression: characters gain Feats at set levels based on their class group — training, cosmic favour, or survival instinct earned through experience
  • Path Tables: drawn from General, Martial, Specialist, or Arcane & Devout, restricted by class
  • Hybrids: can choose from either of their two thematic Paths

See The Feats of Arneyan for the complete Feat Progression table, Path restrictions, and every available Feat.

• What They Are: background, utility, and lore skills that expand what a character can do outside combat
  • Slots: every character starts with 3 NWP slots, gaining 1 more at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, 20th, and 24th level (9 total across a full career)
  • Access: no class restriction on which proficiencies a character can take

See Skills (NWP) for the training-tier rules and the complete Master Proficiency List.

• Common: universal across Veradyna — every people and nation speaks it without exception
  • Ancestry Languages: every ancestry grants one or more languages tied to its heritage, for free
  • Bonus Languages: every character also knows additional languages equal to their Intelligence modifier (minimum 0)
  • Choosing: freely from the Common Tongues (e.g. Dwarvish, Elvish) or, where a class feature, Kit, Patron, or NWP grants access, the rarer Rare Tongues (e.g. Draconic, Infernal, Thieves' Cant)
  • Stacking: ancestry languages sit on top of the Intelligence-modifier pool — they never compete with it
  • Literacy: assumed in any language you know, unless your background says otherwise (GM discretion)
  • NWPs: the Languages, Ancient and Languages, Modern Skills grant additional languages beyond this starting allotment

See Languages of Veradyna for the complete Ancestry Language table and every Common and Rare Tongue.

• What It Covers: your character's moral and ethical outlook across nine combinations of Law/Neutrality/Chaos and Good/Neutrality/Evil
  • Not a Restriction: a roleplay guideline — no class, Kit, Feat Path, or multiclass combination requires or forbids any alignment
  • Where It Matters: certain spells and magic items key off alignment, alignment-based deities respond to how closely a worshipper matches their outlook, and outsiders or fiends may react to your declared alignment

See Alignment in Arneyan for the complete breakdown.

• Starting Gold: roll based on your class category (5d4 for a Monk up to 3d6×10 for the wealthiest martial and divine classes)
  • Shopping: spend it using the Shopkeeper's Catalogue
  • Carrying Capacity: a Strength-scaled inventory grid (18 slots baseline, 20 at Strength 16+, 16 at Strength 6 or less) rather than weight
  • Quick Start: a curated Basic Necessities list, common starting weapons, and six pre-built Starting Packs

See Starting Equipment & Gear for all of it, plus where to find full pricing on everything else.

Multiclassing

Arneyan Campaign Setting

The Basics

Decision Point: Multiclassing must be chosen at character creation, not added retroactively, unless the GM approves an in-fiction reason (training under a mentor, a life-changing event, etc.).

Combinations: Any ancestry may combine any number of classes — the only requirement is a score of 13+ in each combined class's Key Attribute. Nothing stops any ancestry from combining 3 or more classes if the stats are there.

No Alignment Restriction: Choose any alignment for any class or class combination.

Attribute Requirement: You must have a score of 13+ in each combined class's key Attribute.

Arneyan Ancestries

Stats & Mechanics Reference

A mechanics-first reference. Every ancestry below lists its size, speed, darkvision, and attribute bonus/penalty in a single summary line, followed by its complete set of innate traits.

Sub-type entries add to the ancestry's base traits rather than replacing them, and use identical stats to their parent ancestry unless noted otherwise. A sub-type is never a separate attribute-bonus line of its own — choose it for flavour and the listed bonus traits, not a different stat spread, except where Genasi and Shifter are called out below, since their castes/lineages carry their own attribute bonus.

Weapon and armour training from an ancestry adds those weapons to your class's list and removes the penalties for wearing that armour. It never lets a class that lists "None" for armour cast in it.

Where an ancestry trait forces a saving throw without stating a DC, the DC is 10 + half your level (minimum 1) + the modifier of the stated attribute (Level is character level). Unless a trait says otherwise, this uses Constitution for breath, poison and bite effects and Strength for grapple, knockdown and shove effects. This is the Ancestry Save DC.

Aasimar

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Wis / +1 Cha, −1 Str

Traits

  • Resistance 5 to necrotic & radiant. 1/long rest: bright light 10ft radius (illumination only). 1/long rest: Lay on Hands heal = character level.
  • Advantage on saves vs frightened.
  • Choose one Wisdom or Charisma skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and does not take an NWP slot.

Automaton

Size Small / Medium / Large (chosen at creation) • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Con / +1 Int, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Immune to effects targeting biological creatures, including poison and disease (still healed by magic, still affected mentally); doesn't need to breathe or sleep, though a long rest is still required (low-power idle).
  • Advantage on Strength checks to force/break/overpower.
  • Choose one Craft or Engineering skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and does not take an NWP slot.

Subtypes

  • 1st Generation: +1 natural armour AC, Advantage on saves vs forced shutdown/disable/override.
  • 2nd Generation and later: Choose one additional Craft, Engineering or precision skill; you have Advantage on checks with it (two chosen skills in total), plus Modular Repair (field maintenance, 1/long rest; restore 1d8 + Constitution modifier HP; 1 Luck for a second use).

Bugbear

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Dex, −1 Int

Traits

  • +5ft reach on melee attacks.
  • Once per encounter, bonus damage = character level vs a creature that hasn't acted yet (1 Luck for a second trigger per encounter).
  • Advantage on Stealth checks despite size.
  • Weapon training: morningstar, javelin, light crossbow, greatclub.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Changeling

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Cha / +1 Dex, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Shapechanger: alter appearance to any similar-size humanoid as an action (clothing/gear unaffected).
  • Advantage on checks to imitate a specific voice/mannerism once observed.
  • Advantage on saves vs charmed.
  • Advantage on Insight checks to detect deception aimed at them.
  • Perfect Mask: 1/long rest, your assumed disguise becomes undetectable for one scene, resisting even magical discernment (1 Luck for a second use).

Deep Gnomes (Svirfneblin)

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision 120ft • +2 Int / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Advantage on Stealth in stone/rocky terrain.
  • Innate Nondetection (self only), 1/long rest, lasting 8 hours.
  • Innate Blindness/Deafness 1/day (Fortitude save, Ancestry Save DC, Constitution).
  • Advantage on Will saves vs magic.
  • Weapon training: dagger, light hammer, heavy pick, hand crossbow.

Dragonborn

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Cha, −1 Dex

Traits

  • Draconic type: choose fire, cold, lightning, poison or acid at creation. 1/long rest breath weapon of that type: line or cone, damage = character level, Reflex save for half (Ancestry Save DC, Constitution; 1 Luck for an extra use).
  • Resistance 5 to your draconic type.
  • Advantage on Charisma checks towards other dragon-kin and true dragons.
  • Weapon training: longsword, spear, greatclub, javelin.

Duergar

Size Medium • Speed 25ft (not reduced by armour or encumbrance) • Darkvision 120ft • +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Perception checks in direct sunlight.
  • Advantage on saves vs illusion, charm, and paralysis.
  • Advantage on stonework/underground construction/unusual-stonework checks.
  • Innate Invisibility, 1/day, until you attack or cast, or up to 1 minute (1 Luck for a second use, or to cast Enlarge instead).
  • Weapon training: warhammer, handaxe, light crossbow, heavy pick.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Dwarf

Size Medium • Speed 25ft (not reduced by armour or encumbrance) • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Advantage on stonework/underground construction/unusual-stonework checks.
  • Advantage on saves vs poison; Resistance 5 to poison damage.
  • Choose one Craft skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and does not take an NWP slot.
  • The Clan Weapon (Disadvantage on Charisma checks with other dwarves if lost, until recovered).
  • Stonebraced: 1/long rest, treat an incoming critical hit as a normal hit, or ignore a knockdown.
  • Weapon training: handaxe, battleaxe, warhammer, light crossbow, firearms.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Subtypes

  • Dul Khagul: Advantage identifying clan lineage/weapon origin/traditions; Advantage on saves vs being charmed or persuaded against clan loyalty.
  • Tenor Hold: Advantage on craft/repair/identify firearms & mechanical devices; Advantage on checks involving human cultures and languages.

Elf

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Low-Light Vision (not true darkvision) • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Con

Traits

  • Immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on saves vs charm.
  • Trance (4hr rest instead of 8hr sleep).
  • Keen Senses: Advantage on Perception checks (sight or hearing) and on concentration saves to maintain spells.
  • Armour training: light.

Subtypes

  • High Elf: weapon training (longsword/shortsword/longbow/rapier), one Wizard cantrip at creation, Arcane Sense (innately sense the presence and rough direction of significant magical auras or arcane sites — wards, ley-adjacent places, active enchantments — within 60ft, no check required).
  • Saevren (Wood Elf): weapon training (longbow/shortbow/shortsword/handaxe), +5ft speed, Advantage on Stealth/Perception in natural environments, Camouflage (1/long rest, as part of your movement while in natural terrain: become undetectable to passive notice until you move or act).
  • Iiria Elf (Jinia coastal): weapon training (shortsword/longbow/spear/net), Advantage on checks/saves involving navigation/sailing/coastal environments, Advantage on Perception at sea or on coastlines, Sea Legs (1/long rest: reroll a failed Reflex save while aboard a vessel or in open water).

Firbolg

Size Large • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Hardy (Advantage on Fortitude saves against disease and harsh weather).
  • Powerful Build (Advantage on Strength checks to push, drag or lift).
  • Speech of Beast and Leaf (simple communication with beasts/plants). 1/long rest: invisible as part of your movement until you attack or cast, or until the end of your next turn (1 Luck for extra use).
  • Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to live off the land or avoid detection travelling.
  • Weapon training: club, staff, spear, sling.

Genasi

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • Constitution + caste attribute (see below)

  • Fire: +2 Con / +1 Cha, −1 Wis
  • Earth: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Cha
  • Water: +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Dex
  • Air: +2 Con / +1 Dex, −1 Str

Traits

  • Resistance 5 to a damage type by caste.
  • Doesn't need to breathe; can hold breath indefinitely.
  • One Sorcerer cantrip themed to caste at creation.
  • Castes: Fire — Charisma-themed, resist fire, Advantage on illusion/storytelling checks.
  • Earth — Strength-themed, resist poison, Advantage on stonework/mountainous-terrain checks.
  • Water — Wisdom-themed, resist cold, Advantage on swimming/sailing/open-water checks.
  • Air — Dexterity-themed, resist lightning, Advantage on balance/falling/sudden-movement checks.

Gnome

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Int / +1 Dex, −1 Str

Traits

  • Advantage on Will saves vs magic.
  • Chosen Expertise: Advantage on all checks with one chosen skill/craft, including building, repairing, or identifying small mechanical devices even outside that skill.
  • Advantage on Intelligence checks to solve a puzzle/riddle/mechanism under time pressure.
  • Advantage on checks to hide or squeeze through tight spaces despite encumbrance.
  • Clever Fallback: 1/long rest, reroll any one failed Intelligence check (1 Luck for a second use).
  • Weapon training: dagger, light hammer, hand crossbow, sling.

Subtypes

  • Tariel Gnome: Charisma-themed, Advantage on Charisma checks towards human communities, Advantage on trade/craft-commission/small-business checks.
  • Mournas Gnome: Constitution-themed, Advantage on saves vs frightened, Advantage on checks involving Mournas civic structure/remembrance/community organising.
  • Veradyna Gnome: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Survival/Stealth within Veradyna's wilderness, Advantage on checks navigating/understanding Veradyna's native political landscape.

Goblin

Size Small • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Dex / +1 Con, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Mob Tactics: Advantage on your first attack roll each round against a creature that has two or more of your allies adjacent to it. 1/long rest, bonus damage = character level when damaging a larger creature (1 Luck for extra use).
  • Choose one skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and does not take an NWP slot.
  • Weapon training: shortsword, shortbow, sling, dagger.
  • Armour training: light.

Goliath

Size Large • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Int

Traits

  • Advantage on Strength checks to push, drag, lift or break against a smaller creature or object.
  • Resistance 5 to cold.
  • Mountain Endurance (Advantage on Fortitude saves against exhaustion, forced marching and thin mountain air). 1/long rest, when hit: reduce the damage by 1d12 + Constitution modifier (1 Luck for extra use).
  • Weapon training: two-handed axe, maul, javelin, greatclub.

Subtypes

  • Jotunas Goliath: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Jotunas terrain/tribal-custom/true-giant-lineage checks, Advantage on Charisma checks towards Dul Khagul dwarves.
  • Tribe Greater Goliath (Strongroar Lands): Charisma-themed, Advantage on Strongroar Lands terrain/custom checks, Advantage on Charisma checks towards Tenor Hold dwarves.

Half-Elf

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Low-Light Vision (not true darkvision) • +2 Cha / +1 Dex, no penalty

Traits

  • Immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on saves vs charm.
  • Flexible Rest: fully rested from either a 4hr trance or 8hr sleep.
  • Choose one additional skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and does not take an NWP slot.
  • Advantage on social checks with both humans and elves.
  • Dual Heritage: 1/long rest, reroll any one failed save or check (1 Luck for a second use).
  • Weapon training: longsword, shortsword, longbow, plus one martial weapon of choice.
  • Armour training: light.

Half-Orc

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Relentless Endurance: 1/day, when damage of any kind would drop you to 0 HP or below, drop to 1 HP instead.
  • Choose one additional skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and does not take an NWP slot.
  • Brutal Strikes: on a critical hit, add one extra damage die of the weapon's type (passive, always on).
  • Onslaught: 1/long rest, spend 1 Luck to make one additional weapon attack, as part of the same action, against a creature you've just damaged (always costs 1 Luck; there is no free use).
  • Weapon training: two-handed axe, battleaxe, javelin, handaxe.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Halfling

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision None • +2 Dex / +1 Cha, −1 Str

Traits

  • Lucky: on a natural 1 (attack, ability check, or save), reroll and must take the new result, up to 3 times per session. A Halfling who takes the Lucky feat has 4 in all.
  • Nimble: can move through the space of any larger creature.
  • Advantage on checks related to farming, foraging, or identifying plants.
  • Brave Heart: 1/long rest, before you roll a save, gain Advantage on it (1 Luck for an extra use).
  • Weapon training: sling, shortsword, dagger, handaxe.

Hobgoblin

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Int, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Advantage on checks and saves to resist being frightened.
  • Advantage on Intelligence checks involving strategy, formation tactics, and reading a battlefield.
  • Fortune's Favour: 1/long rest, grant yourself or an ally within 30ft Advantage on an attack roll or save (1 Luck for a second use).
  • Weapon training: longsword, longbow, glaive, light crossbow.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Human

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision None • +1 / +1 to any two attributes of choice, no penalty

Traits

  • Choose one skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and does not take an NWP slot. It keeps its Advantage if you later train or master the skill.
  • Gains an additional Feat from the General Path (The Survivors) at 1st level, on top of their normal 1st-level Feat choice. It follows the usual prerequisites, and can't be a Feat you already have.
  • Weapon training: any two martial weapons of choice.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Kobold

Size Small • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 90ft • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Str

Traits

  • Pack Loyalty: Advantage on your first melee attack each round vs a creature an ally has damaged since your last turn.
  • Advantage on hide/squeeze/tactical-use-of-small-size checks.
  • Trapwise: Advantage on building/identifying/disarming/avoiding mechanical traps.
  • Disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Perception checks in direct sunlight.
  • Advantage on identifying dragon/dragon-kin lineage and on Charisma checks towards true dragons/other dragon-kin.

Subtypes

  • Depsopteron-born (currently bonded): Advantage on mining/tunnel-maintenance/serving-clan-customs checks; Advantage on saves vs compulsion or charm effects imposed by their own bonded dragon/clan (resisting the hand that holds the leash); Disadvantage on Charisma checks against their own bonded dragon/clan while in active service.
  • Komodo Isle (free-born or escaped): Advantage on Survival/navigation in jungle or island terrain; Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated/compelled.

Lizardfolk

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Int

Traits

  • Hold Breath up to 15 minutes. +1 natural armour AC. Advantage on Survival checks to track or forage in swamp/marsh/jungle terrain.
  • Bite unarmed strike: 1d4 + Strength modifier.
  • Swamp's Grip: 1/long rest, a successful bite also grapples the target, which must make a Fortitude save (Ancestry Save DC, Strength) or be restrained until the end of your next turn, no extra action required.
  • Advantage on Charisma checks towards other dragon-kin and true dragons.

Subtypes

  • East Depsopteron: Charisma-themed, Advantage on Aurethys customs/metallic-dragon-hierarchy checks, Advantage on saves vs fear.
  • West Depsopteron: Strength-themed, Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated, Advantage on checks enduring/surviving harsh labour.
  • Komodo Isle: Dexterity-themed, Advantage on Survival/navigation in jungle/island terrain, Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated/compelled.
  • Veradyna Marsh: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Stealth/Survival specifically in marsh/wetland terrain, Advantage on checks involving Veradyna's native political landscape and tribal customs.

Mindryath

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Wis / +1 Cha, −1 Str

Traits

  • Advantage on saves vs charmed; immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on checks involving nature, plant growth, or communicating with fey/forest-dwelling creatures.
  • Roving Grace: 1/long rest, cross between the Feywild and the material plane without a portal or ritual, arriving at a place you have seen; you cannot bring passengers.
  • One Druid cantrip at creation.
  • Weapon training: staff, sickle, shortbow, dagger.

Minotaur

Size Large • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Int

Traits

  • Horns unarmed strike: 1d8 + Strength modifier.
  • Powerful Build (Advantage on Strength checks to push, drag or lift).
  • Labyrinthine Recall: never lost, always recalls a maze-like layout travelled once.
  • Goring Charge: +1d6 damage on a Horns hit if moved 10ft+ in a straight line first.
  • Weapon training: battleaxe, two-handed axe, javelin, spear.

Subtypes

  • Red Waste/Veradyna: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Survival in harsh/arid/wild terrain, Advantage on Intimidation checks.
  • Tenor Hold: Intelligence-themed, Advantage on Tenor Hold customs/craft/civic-life checks, Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated specifically by fiendish/demonic influence.
  • Opal: Charisma-themed, Advantage on trade/negotiation/Opal-port-culture checks, Advantage on Charisma checks towards other integrating/non-native peoples in Opal.
  • Mournas: Advantage on saves vs frightened, Advantage on checks related to Mournas's civic structure/culture of remembrance, Advantage on Charisma checks towards Mournas's other freed populations.

Nu'Dravi (Drow)

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 120ft • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on saves vs charm.
  • Trance (4hr rest).
  • Advantage on Perception (sight/hearing) in low light or darkness.
  • Innate Dancing Lights at will; Darkness or Faerie Fire, 1/day (choose one when cast; Faerie Fire allows a Reflex save, Ancestry Save DC, Charisma).
  • Weapon training: hand crossbow, shortsword, rapier.
  • Armour training: light.
  • Sunlight Sensitivity varies by faith: Nu'Dravi who worship Eilistraee are exempt entirely.
  • Nu'Dravi of no faith or a neutral faith get a lesser version (Disadvantage only in the first hour of direct sunlight exposure per day).
  • Drow who worship Lolth keep full Sunlight Sensitivity (disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Perception checks in direct sunlight).

Orc

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Int

Traits

  • Relentless Endurance: 1/day, when damage of any kind would drop you to 0 HP or below, drop to 1 HP instead.
  • When wielding a weapon two-handed, reroll any 1s on its damage dice once (keep the new result).
  • Advantage on Intimidation checks. 1/long rest, before you roll: Advantage on an attack roll or Strength check (1 Luck for extra use).
  • Weapon training: two-handed axe, battleaxe, javelin, handaxe.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Shifter

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Low-Light Vision (not true darkvision) • Constitution + lineage attribute (see below)

  • Canidae-Longtooth: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Int
  • Canidae-Wildhunt: +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Str
  • Felidae-Swiftstride: +2 Con / +1 Dex, −1 Wis
  • Ursidae-Beasthide: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Dex
  • Suidae-Gorebrute: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Cha
  • Ophidian-Sslyth: +2 Con / +1 Cha, −1 Int

Traits

  • The Beast Within (Shifting): number of uses/day = half level rounded up (min 1), each lasting a number of rounds = Constitution modifier (min 1).
  • Lineage benefits apply only while shifted.
  • Lineages: Canidae-Longtooth (Pack Attacker) — Strength-themed; shifted: Advantage on your first melee attack roll each round against a creature an ally also threatens.
  • Canidae-Wildhunt (Tracker) — Wisdom-themed; shifted: Advantage on Perception/Survival involving scent or tracking.
  • Felidae-Swiftstride (Skirmisher, covers Catfolk) — Dexterity-themed; shifted: +15ft speed.
  • Ursidae-Beasthide (Stoic Tank) — Constitution-themed; shifted: Resistance 3 to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing, plus temporary HP equal to Constitution modifier each time you shift.
  • Suidae-Gorebrute (Juggernaut/Disruptor) — Strength-themed; shifted: may move through an enemy's space, forcing it to make a Fortitude save (Ancestry Save DC, Strength) or be knocked prone; once per creature per turn, and only creatures no more than one size larger.
  • Ophidian-Sslyth (Ambusher/Controller) — Charisma-themed; shifted: bite manifests venom (a successful unarmed bite forces a Fortitude save (Ancestry Save DC, Constitution) or the target is poisoned for the shift's duration).

Tiefling

"Tiefling" is what others call them. A tiefling is born into a family of another ancestry, human, orc, elf or any other, whose bloodline carries a fiendish curse. The mark can skip generations and appear in a child of ordinary-looking parents. There is no tiefling people, homeland or culture.

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Cha / +1 Int, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Family: choose the ancestry of the family you were born into. You speak its language, and others treat you as one of its people once they look past the marks. Your size, speed, vision and traits are the Tiefling's, whatever your family.
  • Resistance 5 to a damage type set by your bloodline.
  • One Warlock cantrip at creation.
  • Fiendish Retort: 1/long rest, when damaged by a creature within 30ft, unleash it back at them as part of your action on your next turn. The damage type is set by your bloodline: 1d6 at 1st, 1d8 at 5th, 2d6 at 9th, 2d8 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th, 3d8 at 24th.
  • From 11th level, Fiendish Retort can be used twice per long rest.

Bloodlines

  • Infernal (devils): horns, a tail, embers in the eyes. Resist fire; Retort deals fire. Advantage on checks to read, recall or find loopholes in contracts, oaths and bargains. You know Infernal.
  • Abyssal (demons): wild, twisted features that rarely look the same twice in a family. Resist poison; Retort deals acid. Advantage on Charisma checks to intimidate. You know Abyssal.
  • Outer (daemons, rakshasa and stranger fiends): subtle, unsettling marks that are hard to place. Resist necrotic; Retort deals necrotic. Advantage on checks to see through disguises and illusions. You know Infernal or Abyssal.
  • Shadowfell (fiends of shadow): ashen skin, a shadow that moves a moment late. Resist cold; Retort deals cold. Advantage on checks to hide in dim light or darkness. You know Infernal or Abyssal.

Ysoki

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Con

Traits

  • Advantage on Perception checks involving smell or hearing.
  • Cheek Pouch: stash small non-weapon items, retrieve without using an action.
  • Bite unarmed strike: 1d4 + Strength modifier.
  • Nimble Escape: after you attack, you may Disengage or Hide as part of the same action.
  • Advantage on checks to navigate tunnels, sewers, and other confined underground spaces.
  • Weapon training: dagger, hand crossbow, sling, shortsword.

Ancestries grant a classic fixed attribute bonus/penalty pair: a +2 to a primary attribute, a +1 to a secondary attribute, and (for most ancestries) a −1 penalty to a third. Human is the exception, granting +1/+1 to any two attributes of the player's choice with no penalty.

  • Ancestry Attribute Trade-Off (optional rule): any ancestry with a penalty may remove that −1 penalty by downgrading its +2 bonus to a +1 instead. This is an either/or choice made once, at creation — full bonus plus penalty, or a smaller flat bonus with no penalty. It never applies to ancestries with no penalty to begin with (Human, Half-Elf). This is a one-time choice made at character creation and does not change if you later change ancestry via a retcon mid-campaign at the GM's discretion.
  • Sub-types: use identical stats to their parent ancestry. A sub-type never changes which attributes are bonused or penalised — regional and cultural variants (the Gnome cultures, Elf cultures, Dwarf clans, and so on) are differentiated entirely by their flavour traits and Advantages, never by different stats. The exception is Shifter lineages and Genasi castes, which aren't cultural sub-types in this sense — their secondary stat is the ancestry's own built-in variable, so each lineage or caste is a normal base-ancestry stat line in its own right, the same way Human's bonus is player-chosen rather than fixed.

This is a stats-only reference. Lore, origins, and setting placement are intentionally left out, apart from the Tiefling's opening line; see the Arneyan setting material for those.

  • Sub-type Entries: add to the ancestry's base traits rather than replacing them — a Dul Khagul Dwarf, for instance, still has all of the base Dwarf's traits (stonework Advantage, poison Advantage and Resistance, chosen Craft skill, Clan Weapon) plus its own two Dul Khagul-specific Advantages

pages.name: How Attributes Work in This System

text.content:
Arneyan uses six core attributes — Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma — plus Luck as a separate seventh stat (see The Luck Stat reference). Each attribute has a raw score, generated using Method V below, and that score converts to a modifier that gets added to relevant rolls.

The Arneyan Modifier Table

Every attribute score converts to a modifier on this table. Monsters use the same table.

ScoreModifierScoreModifier
0Helpless or dead18+3
1–2−419–20+4
3−321–22+5
4–5−223–25+6
6–8−126–27+7
9–12+028–29+8
13–15+130+9
16–17+2

Rolled scores. Method V never produces a score above 18, and no score starts above 18 (see Starting Scores).

20 is the cap for mortals. Ancestry, feats and every other ordinary source can raise a score to 20 and no further. The only exception is a class's permanent attribute reward, which can carry a score to 22. Anything higher takes an extraordinary source such as legendary magic or a god's blessing; see The Mortal Limit. Scores above 22 belong to monsters, gods and legends.

What the Attributes Do

Strength: melee attack and damage, thrown and Strength-based weapons, carrying capacity (18 slots, 20 at Strength 16+, 16 at 6 or less; see Inventory & Carrying Capacity in Book I), and feats of force.

Dexterity: Armour Class (within your armour's limit), initiative, ranged attack and damage, Finesse weapons, Reflex saves, and agility and stealth.

Constitution: Hit Points, Fortitude saves, endurance, and resisting poison and disease.

Intelligence: extra languages, lore, and the key attribute for Wizards, Illusionists, Necromancers, Magi and Artificers.

Wisdom: Will saves, awareness, insight and survival instincts, and the key attribute for Clerics, Druids and Witches.

Charisma: persuasion, deception, leadership, henchmen and hirelings, and the key attribute for Bards, Knights, Paladins, Sorcerers and Warlocks.

The Mortal Limit

The Cap. No attribute can exceed 20. Ancestry bonuses, Feat bonuses and every other ordinary source stop at 20, and any excess is lost. The one exception is the permanent attribute bonus a class grants as a level reward (such as +1 at 15th level): a class bonus can carry an attribute past 20, up to a maximum of 22.

Beyond Mortal Limits. Only extraordinary events lift a score past its cap: legendary magic (a wish of the highest order, an ancient tome, a relic of power), a god's blessing earned through deeds or devotion, or a bargain struck with a devil, a fey lord or another patron. The GM decides what is granted and sets the price. A blessing can be withdrawn if you break faith, and a bargain is collected on when it suits the other party. Note the source beside the score on your sheet: if the source ends, so does the boost. Such a boost is added after the cap and uses the same modifier table, so a score of 23 gives +6. The table ends at 30, a limit no mortal reaches.

How Advantage Works

Advantage comes from GM discretion (situational), from Master training in an NWP (see Skills), from ancestry or class traits, manoeuvres and positioning (charging, flanking), and from other effects where listed. Roll two d20 and take the higher. Advantage and Disadvantage do not stack: any number of sources of one kind gives a single extra die, and one source of each cancels out so you roll one d20. Advantage never applies to damage rolls.

Ancestry Attribute Bonuses

Every ancestry grants a fixed attribute bonus/penalty pair: a +2 to a primary attribute, a +1 to a secondary attribute, and (for most ancestries) a −1 penalty to a third. Human instead gets +1/+1 to any two attributes of the player's choice, with no penalty. See the Ancestries reference for the full table.

Dice Set: six scores, one for each attribute. You roll two separate sets (Set Alpha and Set Beta) and keep one of them whole.

Method V

Roll six pools of d6s in this order. For each pool, add the three highest dice to get one score.

  • Pool 1: roll 8d6, keep the highest 3
  • Pool 2: roll 5d6, keep the highest 3
  • Pool 3: roll 4d6, keep the highest 3
  • Pools 4, 5 and 6: roll 3d6 each, keep all 3

The six scores are Set Alpha. Roll all six pools again to make Set Beta. Choose one set to keep and assign its six scores to your attributes however you wish. The set you do not keep may be donated to the table (Rule B).

Three table rules keep rolling fair and make sure no player is left with an unplayable hero.

Rule A: The Two-Set Choice (No Cherry-Picking)

You keep one entire set. You cannot swap individual scores between your two sets.

  • Illegal: Set Alpha is 18, 14, 13, 11, 10, 6 and Set Beta is 15, 14, 14, 12, 11, 10. You cannot take the 18 from Alpha and swap its 6 for a 10 from Beta.
  • Legal: take Set Alpha exactly as it is (the 18, but also the 6), or Set Beta exactly as it is (no 18, but no weakness).

Rule B: The Table Donation Rule

If you roll two good sets, keep your favourite and write the other on the whiteboard as a donation to the table. Any player whose own sets are poor can take a donated set instead of their own.

  • Example: Tamla rolls two good sets, keeps the better one for her Rogue and donates the other (16, 15, 14, 13, 11, 10). Alex rolls nothing above a 12, discards his own sets and builds his Paladin from Tamla's.

Rule C: The Gygaxian Threshold

A hero needs at least two scores of 14 or higher in the chosen set, before ancestry bonuses. If neither of your sets qualifies and no donated set is available, discard both and roll both sets again.

  • Example: Alex's Set Alpha is 13, 13, 12, 11, 9, 8 (no score of 14 or higher) and Set Beta is 14, 13, 11, 10, 10, 7 (only one). Both fail, so unless someone has donated a set, he rolls again.

Optional Rule: The Quick Roll

For a table that prefers a simpler roll, the GM may allow 4d6 instead of Method V. Roll 4d6 six times, dropping the lowest die each time, and assign the six results to your attributes as you like. Rule C still applies (two scores of 14 or higher, or roll again), and so does the starting cap of 18.

The starting cap. When a character is created, no score can go above 18, even after ancestry bonuses and feats. The cap applies at any starting level; attribute rewards from levels above 1st are added afterwards, and from then on scores follow The Mortal Limit.

Moving the excess. If your ancestry bonus, or an attribute bonus from a feat taken at creation (such as Steady Hand), would take a score above 18, put the points that would be lost into another attribute of your choice instead. That attribute also stops at 18.

Example 1: A Balanced Set

Alex rolls his pools in order: 8d6 (6,6,5,5,4,2,1,1 keeps 6,6,5 = 17); 5d6 (6,5,4,3,2 keeps 6,5,4 = 15); 4d6 (5,5,4,2 keeps 5,5,4 = 14); 3d6 (6,4,2 = 12); 3d6 (5,3,3 = 11); 3d6 (4,3,2 = 9). Set Alpha is 17, 15, 14, 12, 11, 9, which clears the Gygaxian Threshold. His Set Beta is 15, 13, 12, 11, 10, 8, so he keeps Set Alpha for a sharp-witted Wizard.

Example 2: A Big Score and a Big Flaw

Tamla's Set Alpha is 18, 16, 14, 11, 10, 4; her last 3d6 pool came up 2, 1, 1. She puts the 18 in Dexterity, the 16 in Intelligence and the 4 in Constitution: a brilliant marksman with a frail body. Her ancestry gives +2 Dexterity, which would take the 18 past the cap, so she moves both points to Intelligence instead (16 becomes 18).

Example 3: The Cursed Roller

Both of Alex's sets fail the Gygaxian Threshold (see Rule C). Tamla has a spare set (16, 15, 14, 13, 11, 10) and donates it, so Alex builds a strong frontline Paladin from it instead of rolling again.

The 8d6 pool averages about 15, the 5d6 about 13, the 4d6 about 12 and each 3d6 about 10½. About one set in five has a natural 18, so roughly one hero in three can choose a set with one, and about one player in seventeen fails the Gygaxian Threshold on both sets and needs a donated set or a fresh roll.
• Starting Score: roll 4d6 and drop the lowest — this is your Starting Luck Score, set at character creation

• Spend: spend points of Luck to add a +1 bonus per point to a d20 roll (attack rolls, saving throws, ability or skill checks; never damage rolls)
  • The Declaration: you must declare you are burning Luck after you roll, but before the GM describes the outcome
  • The Cost: your Current Luck Score decreases by the amount spent; your Starting Luck remains the same

Occasionally, the GM will call for a Luck Check to see if fate is on your side (e.g. “Do you find a dry spot to camp?” or “Does the monster target you?”).

  • Succeeding: roll a d20 equal to or lower than your Current Luck Score. A natural 1 always succeeds and a natural 20 always fails, whatever your Luck
  • The Catch: as you burn Luck for bonuses, your chances of succeeding on these checks decrease — fate turning its back on you

When a character is reduced to 0 HP, they fall unconscious but stable; below 0 HP they begin dying (see Death & Dying in The Arneyan Codex). Luck can provide a narrow window of survival.

  • The Last Chance: a dying character can choose to burn 1 point of Luck to attempt to stabilise
  • The Check: make an immediate stabilisation roll, a Fortitude save (DC 10). On a success the character stops dying and is stabilised, still unconscious at their current HP. On a failure they continue dying as normal. The First Aid cantrip stabilises a dying creature without a roll

Luck does not recover with sleep or rest. In the harsh world of Arneyan, you must earn your favour back.

  • Alignment Actions: performing a significant deed that furthers the goals of your declared Alignment may earn +1 Luck at the GM's discretion (once per session at most)
  • Levelling Up: upon reaching a new level, you recover 1 Luck point
  • Maximum: Luck can never exceed 20. The Luck-raising Feats (Fated Survivor, Lucky, Luck Battery, Skilled Regeneration) are explicit exceptions to the recovery rules above

Luck is a double-edged sword. A player who burns 5 points of Luck to land a killing blow on a boss might find themselves unable to pass a Luck check to avoid a pit trap ten minutes later. Remind your players: the more you lean on Fate, the faster she steps aside.

Every level costs the same XP, set by your class (see How Levels Are Awarded in The Arneyan Codex). When your XP reaches your rate, spend it to gain a level; anything left over carries towards the next, but one award never gives more than one level. You begin at 1st level, so 5th takes four fills and 24th takes twenty-three. A multiclass character pays the highest rate among their classes, plus 2 XP per level for each class beyond the first.

XP per LevelClasses
8Assassin, Rogue
10Archer, Artificer, Barbarian, Bard, Cleric, Druid, Fighter, Gunslinger, Illusionist, Knight, Magus, Monk, Ranger, Sorcerer, Swashbuckler, Warlock
12Battle Priest (Cleric), Necromancer, Paladin, Witch, Wizard

Class GroupProgression Levels
Fighters1st, 3rd, 6th, 11th, 15th, 20th
Barbarians, Bards, Paladins, Knights, Monks, Artificers, Magi1st, 2nd, 6th, 12th, 16th, 21st
Clerics, Druids, Illusionists, Wizards, Sorcerers, Warlocks, Witches, Necromancers1st, 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, 20th
Assassins, Rogues, Rangers, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers1st, 2nd, 6th, 11th, 16th, 21st

Path Restrictions: Your class directly determines which specific Path table you can choose from.

Pure Classes: Must choose from their designated Path list or the General Path.

Half-Casters & Hybrids: Bards, Paladins, Rangers, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers, Rogues, Assassins, Monks, Artificers, and Magi naturally bridge two worlds and may choose from either of their thematic paths without needing to multiclass:

  • Bard — Martial or Arcane & Devout
  • Paladin — Martial or Arcane & Devout
  • Ranger — Martial or Specialist
  • Archer — Martial or Specialist
  • Rogue — Martial or Specialist
  • Assassin — Martial or Specialist
  • Monk — Martial or Specialist
  • Gunslinger — Martial or Specialist
  • Swashbuckler — Martial or Specialist
  • Artificer — Specialist or Arcane & Devout
  • Magus — Martial or Arcane & Devout

Multiclassing Access: The only way a pure class can gain access to multiple restricted Path tables. When you gain a Feat level, you may choose from the Path of any class you hold levels in.

Taking Feats: Each feat can be taken only once unless its entry says otherwise. A feat and a class feature of the same name do not stack; use the better.

Custom Feats: Alternatively, any character can work with the GM to design a custom Feat tailored directly to their character's story, current capabilities, and class lore.

Attribute Bonuses: an attribute bonus from a Feat cannot take a score above 20, and bonuses from different Feats do not stack past that limit. See The Mortal Limit.

I. General Path (The Survivors)

Open to all classes by default.

Fated Survivor and Lucky (here), and Luck Battery and Skilled Regeneration (Specialist Path), are explicit exceptions to the normal Luck recovery rules; no other Feat changes how Luck is gained or recovered. Luck can never exceed 20.

Diehard Once per session, if reduced to 0 HP or below, spend 2 points of Luck to instantly remain at 1 HP and stay conscious.

Fated Survivor Your Current Luck can never be burned below 1. Gain +1 to your Starting Luck Score immediately upon taking this Feat, with further +1 increases at each of 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level reached after taking it (your Current Luck rises by the same amount, to a maximum of 20).

Inscrutable Fate Once per session, when hit, spend 2 points of Luck to force a reroll (lower result used). Gain Advantage on Luck Checks against traps (roll twice and take the lower d20, since low is good on a Luck Check).

Lucky When you gain a level, recover 1d4+1 Luck instead of 1 (to a maximum of 20). If Luck Battery also applies, use the higher. Reroll one Natural 1, once per session (a Halfling adds this to the ancestry's 3, for 4 in all).

Battlefield Medic Treat wounds (Wisdom check, DC 15, Hard tier) to heal a target for HP equal to your Level + your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1). A healer can treat each target only once per day.

Quick Recovery Once per session, spend 2 Luck to remove one condition (frightened, poisoned, prone, etc.) from yourself at the start of your turn.

Toughness (Constitution) Gain +1 Max HP per level (retroactive). Gain +1 to Constitution (once, on taking this feat). Advantage on Constitution-based checks.

Iron Constitution (Constitution) Advantage on saving throws against poison and disease. Gain +1 to Constitution (once, on taking this feat).

Will of Iron (Wisdom / Intelligence / Charisma — choose one for the stat bump) Permanent +2 bonus to Will saving throws. Gain +1 to one of Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma of your choice (once, on taking this feat).

Steady Hand (Strength / Dexterity — choose one for the stat bump) Advantage on checks made to resist being disarmed, knocked prone, or moved against your will. Gain +1 to Strength or Dexterity of your choice (once, on taking this feat).

Brute Force (Strength) Advantage on Strength checks made to break, force open, or physically overpower an obstacle. Gain +1 to Strength (once, on taking this feat).

Swift Reflexes (Dexterity) Advantage on Initiative rolls. Gain +1 to Dexterity (once, on taking this feat).

Keen Mind (Intelligence) Advantage on Intelligence checks made to recall lore, history, or identify unfamiliar creatures and phenomena. Gain +1 to Intelligence (once, on taking this feat).

Perceptive Grit (Wisdom) Advantage on Perception checks made to avoid being surprised or ambushed. Gain +1 to Wisdom (once, on taking this feat).

Charismatic Presence (Charisma) Once per session, as part of your action, grant one ally within earshot Advantage on their next attack roll or ability check. Gain +1 to Charisma (once, on taking this feat).

Skilled Gain two additional NWP slots.

II. Martial Path

Available to: Fighters, Barbarians, Knights, Paladins, Magi, Bards, Rangers, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers, Rogues, Assassins, and Monks.

Armour Master: Gain +1 AC while wearing armour. You are trained in light armour (Padded Armour, Leather Armour and Studded Leather).

Intimidating Presence: Once per encounter, plant yourself and let a single enemy within 10ft feel exactly what they're up against — unless they pass a Will save (DC = 10 + half your level (minimum 1) + your Charisma modifier), they fight the rest of the round flinching, at Disadvantage.

Cleave: Don't stop moving when a blow lands — the momentum carries your weapon on into whoever is next. You may use the Cleave manoeuvre up to twice per turn instead of once (three times a turn with a Cleaving weapon).

Combat Reflexes: Once per round, make an Attack of Opportunity (one melee attack) against an enemy you can see that leaves your melee reach or moves past or through it. Disengage prevents it.

Critical Strike: You are a master of precision. Your weapon attacks score a Critical Hit on a natural 20, or on a natural 19 that hits.

Flowing Strikes: Once per round, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, let the momentum carry through — make one extra melee attack. Against the creature you just hit it is rolled with Disadvantage; against a different creature within your reach it is a normal roll. The extra attack cannot trigger Flowing Strikes again.

Mighty Deed of Arms: Once per round, call your shot before you swing. Roll a d4 alongside your attack; if the hit lands and the d4 comes up 3 or better, choose one: knock the target Prone, disarm it, push it 10ft, blind it until the end of its next turn, or give it Disadvantage on its next attack. The target resists with a save against 10 + half your level (minimum 1) + your Strength modifier: Fortitude against Prone, a push or a disarm, Reflex against blinding, Will against the attack penalty. A creature that saves is immune to your Deeds for the rest of the fight. A creature more than one size larger than you ignores the deed.

Power Attack (Smash): Put everything into the swing with a melee weapon that has the Heavy trait, held in two hands. Trade your usual precision for a strike that lands like a falling tree — roll the attack with Disadvantage (any Advantage you would have on it is ignored, so it can never cancel the Disadvantage), but if it connects, roll one extra weapon damage die and add it to the damage (two extra dice from 10th level). It cannot be combined on the same attack with another option that gives your own attack Disadvantage (Shield Blow).

Shield Bash: Snap your shield forward, a solid crack to the ribs or jaw. Once per round, when you hit a creature no more than one size larger than you with a melee attack while holding a shield, slam the shield in as part of the same attack. The target makes a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + half your level (minimum 1) + your Strength modifier) or is knocked Prone.

Shield Expert: +1 AC while wielding a shield, and add your shield's AC bonus to Reflex saves.

Two-Weapon Fighting: Your off-hand attack no longer suffers Disadvantage. The same feat appears in the Specialist Path; you can only take it once.

Weapon Master: Choose one weapon type. Once per round, reroll one missed attack roll with it, and gain +2 to Damage with it. If you already have a class feature granting weapon specialisation (Fighter), this instead applies to a second weapon of your choice, rather than duplicating your first.

Shove: Once per round, when you land a hit in melee on a creature no more than one size larger than you, you may put your full weight behind the blow: you deal your damage and also shove the target 10ft away from you along the ground. Being shoved never provokes Attacks of Opportunity.

III. Specialist Path

Available to: Rogues, Assassins, Rangers, Monks, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers, and Artificers.

Feint: Fake a step, a stumble, an opening that isn't there. Once per round, in place of one attack, make a Charisma (Deception) or Dexterity check against the target's Wisdom check. Sell it, and they overcommit to defending against a strike that was never coming. On a success, choose one: the target has Disadvantage on its next attack against you, or you have Advantage on your next attack against it.

Alertness: Nothing gets past you unnoticed — not the shift in a shadow, not the change in someone's breathing before they act. You're already moving before most people even register something's wrong. Cannot be surprised by nonmagical means; gain +2 to Initiative rolls. This stacks with Advantage on Initiative from other sources (such as Swift Reflexes or the Swashbuckler's En Garde).

Acrobatics: Halve falling damage; gain Advantage on checks to jump, climb, or manoeuvre. You can move through the spaces of enemies, and your movement never provokes Attacks of Opportunity.

Luck Battery: Once per session, give up to 3 of your Current Luck points to an ally; they are not returned. Recover 2 Luck points instead of 1 upon levelling. If Lucky also applies, use the higher.

Master of Disguise: Advantage on checks to forge, impersonate, or maintain a disguise under scrutiny, and Advantage on the first Deception check made in any encounter. You can put together a convincing disguise in 1 minute, and once per day you may reroll a failed check to maintain a disguise or deception.

Mobile: Base movement increases by +10 feet.

Point-Blank Terror: Most people flinch putting a bow to full draw with an enemy already inside their reach. You don't — you put the shot exactly where you meant to, close enough to feel their breath. No Disadvantage for using ranged weapons within 5ft reach of an enemy.

Predator: You move like something that's done this before — silent, low, patient. And if the strike lands from where they never saw you coming, it lands harder for it. Gain Advantage on Stealth checks. If you have the Sneak Attack ability, your Sneak Attack deals +1d6.

Skilled Regeneration: Once per session, when burning Luck turns a failed roll into a success, regain 1 of the Luck spent.

Two-Weapon Fighting: Two blades moving independently is supposed to get you killed — one always lagging half a beat behind the other. You've closed that gap; both hands work like they belong to the same fight. Your off-hand attack no longer suffers Disadvantage. The same feat as in the Martial Path; you can only take it once.

Steady Aim: No Disadvantage on ranged attacks against a target engaged in melee with an ally.

Sure Footing: Uneven ground, loose rubble, a grip trying to drag you down — none of it slows you. You move like the terrain isn't a factor, and when something tries to pin you in place, you're already halfway out of its grip before it sets. Ignore difficult terrain penalties to movement, and gain Advantage on checks to avoid or escape being restrained, grappled, or knocked prone.

Fate's Reversal: Once per session, when the dice turn on you — or on someone at your side — you can reach out and bend that luck back in your favour. A natural 1 becomes a natural 20, like fate just changed its mind. (Spend 2 Luck; usable on yourself or an ally within 30ft.)

IV. Arcane & Devout Path

Available to: Wizards, Clerics, Druids, Illusionists, Paladins, Magi, Bards, Sorcerers, Warlocks, Witches, Necromancers, and Artificers.

Blood Magic: Cast a spell when you are out of slots by taking 1d6 damage per spell level. You can only do this while your current HP is higher than the most it could cost (6 per spell level). You can do this a number of times per day equal to your casting-stat modifier (minimum 1). It cannot be used to cast healing spells, and the damage cannot be healed by magic until you complete a long rest. The cost cannot be reduced, resisted or soaked by temporary HP — it comes straight off your HP.

Ritual Caster: Not every working needs to be rushed. Given ten quiet minutes and no blade at your throat, you can draw out the same effect as a hasty combat cast — without burning the reserve you'd need in a fight. Any spell of 3rd level or lower that you know, other than a healing spell, and that doesn't require an instantaneous action in combat, can be cast as a 10-minute ritual instead of spending a slot, provided you're not under threat of imminent combat. Each spell can be ritual-cast once per day. Sorcerers cannot take this feat.

Steady Focus: A blow lands, the ground shifts, someone grabs at you mid-casting — and the working holds anyway. You have Advantage on saves made to keep a spell you are casting, or to maintain concentration on one, when you take damage, are shoved or are otherwise forced to react mid-cast. Once per encounter, you may turn one such failed save into a success.

Healer: Your hands know exactly where to press, what to whisper, what the wound actually needs — every restorative working you cast or brew does that much more. Healing spells and brewed potions restore an additional +1 HP per die, and once per day you may cast a healing spell of 3rd level or lower without expending a slot.

Expanded Mind: You gain one additional spell slot of your highest currently available spell level.

Potent Casting: Once a fight, you can put real weight behind a casting — enough that whoever's on the receiving end finds their usual resistance isn't there when they need it most. Once per encounter, when you cast a spell, the target(s) have Disadvantage on their saving throw against it.

Signature Spell: Choose one spell of 3rd level or lower that you can cast. Once per day, you can cast it without expending a slot.

Mystic Insulation: Magic that gets through your guard doesn't get through clean. Once per encounter, when you fail a saving throw against a harmful spell or effect, halve the damage taken from it.

War Caster: Standing in the thick of a fight doesn't rattle you the way it does most spellcasters. You have Advantage on Fortitude saves made to keep a spell you are casting, or to maintain concentration on one, when you take damage. You can perform the somatic components of spells while holding weapons or a shield in one or both hands. Choose one type of Light or Medium armour, or a shield: you are trained in it, so wearing it does not block your casting. (If your class is already trained in it, this last benefit adds nothing.)

Cantrip Mastery: Learn two additional cantrips from your class spell list. Once per round, when you cast a cantrip, add your casting-stat modifier (minimum +1) to its damage or healing when it hits or the target fails its save. It does not stack with Agonising Blast.

Arcane Insight: Sometimes the answer isn't a spell thrown in anger — it's ten minutes of quiet and the right working turned towards a question instead of a target. Once per day, cast any divination-type spell you know as a ritual investigation over 10 minutes without expending a slot, usable outside combat. You also have Advantage on Intelligence checks to identify spells, magic items and magical effects.
Characters can learn specific background, utility, or lore skills that expand what they can do outside of combat without introducing complex modern skill lists.

Proficiency Slots. Every character starts with 3 Non-Weapon Proficiency slots at level 1, gaining 1 additional slot at levels 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 24 (9 total slots by max level).

Training Tiers. NWP training works in three tiers. Untrained: roll a plain d20 with no attribute modifier. Trained (1 slot spent): roll d20 and add the modifier of the skill's attribute; if that modifier is 0 or less, add +1 instead. Master (a second slot spent on the same skill): add the same as Trained and roll with Advantage. At 1st level your 3 starting slots must each go to a different skill — no doubling into Mastery on day one, so the earliest a skill can reach Master is 4th level. A specialised task is not forbidden without the relevant NWP; you simply roll untrained. A Master of a crafting Skill also pays one third of an item's market price instead of half when crafting it (see Downtime: Crafting in Book I).

Expanding Slots. Spending an extra slot on an NWP you already possess is how you reach the Master tier above: your modifier plus Advantage on checks with it.

Standardisation. Every proficiency costs exactly 1 slot, with no class restriction on which proficiencies a character can choose — any character can take any NWP regardless of class.

Everyday Checks. Ordinary actions such as sneaking, noticing things, climbing, reading a person, intimidating or deceiving someone are plain attribute checks and need no NWP. Names like Stealth, Perception or Insight in a trait, feature or Feat are shorthand for that kind of check (Dexterity to sneak, Wisdom to notice or read a person, Charisma to intimidate or deceive). Persuading an NPC is mostly roleplay: the GM calls for a Charisma check only when the outcome is truly in doubt. NWPs cover trades, lore and specialist skills; rolled untrained, they are a plain d20 with no modifier. A skill an ancestry lets you choose can be an NWP or a kind of everyday check.

Tools. Crafting and trade skills need the matching toolkit (see the Toolkits table). With no usable tools you cannot craft; with improvised tools the roll has Disadvantage.

Alignment is described along two axes — Law/Neutrality/Chaos, and Good/Neutrality/Evil — producing nine possible combinations.

• At character creation, write down the alignment you think best fits your character. This is a guideline, not a contract — the GM doesn't police it, and there's no mechanical penalty for acting outside it in the moment
  • Alignment is descriptive, not restrictive: no class, Kit, Feat Path, or multiclass combination requires a specific alignment or excludes any alignment
  • A character's alignment can shift over the course of a campaign through their actions and choices — this is a roleplay event, not something that needs a mechanical trigger

Alignment has no bearing on rules eligibility anywhere in Arneyan, but it is read and reacted to by a handful of specific things in the world:

Spells & Magic Items: Certain spells (Protection from Alignment, Detect Alignment, Magic Circle vs Alignment, and similar) key directly off a target or area's alignment. Some magic items are alignment-restricted or alignment-empowered — a holy weapon might deal bonus damage only to Evil-aligned creatures, for instance.

Deities: Alignment-based deities (most of the Cleric and Paladin patron list) respond to how closely a worshipper's alignment matches their own. A Lawful Good deity's Cleric acting in a way that's flagrantly Chaotic Evil may find their deity's patience — and their Turn Undead, Divine Protection, or granted powers — running thin, at the GM's discretion. This is a roleplay-driven consequence, not an automatic mechanical penalty, unless the class's entry in Book III says otherwise.

Outsiders & Fiends: Creatures with an inherent alignment subtype (celestials, fiends, certain fey) may react to a character's declared or perceived alignment — favourably, warily, or with open hostility — as the GM determines.

Alignment Actions: Alignment has no mechanical trigger beyond the spells and items above and one GM-awarded reward: the GM may award +1 Luck when a character performs a significant deed that furthers their declared alignment, at most once per session.

Treat alignment the way you'd treat a character's stated ideals, bonds, or flaws — it tells everyone at the table who this character is trying to be. Nobody fails a roll for stepping outside it once, but a Paladin who spends a whole campaign acting Chaotic Evil while claiming to be Lawful Good is a conversation for the table, not a rules problem to adjudicate with dice.

Inventory is tracked with a slot grid, not weight. Check what you can actually carry before you buy.

Base capacity: 18 slots, adjusted by Strength — Strength 16+ grants 20 slots total; Strength 6 or less reduces it to 16 slots total; anything in between stays at the 18-slot baseline.

  • Standard gear: 1 slot
  • Heavy or two-handed items: 2-3 slots
  • Ammunition: 30 per slot
  • Coins: 100 per slot
  • Minor/light items (ink, quills, wax, scrolls, gems of the same tier): bundle up to 5 per slot
  • A Backpack provides the grid itself, takes no slot, and is usually the first thing anyone buys
  • Worn and Wielded: armour you wear, shields and weapons you carry all count against your slots.
  • Over the Limit: while you carry more than your capacity, your speed drops 10ft at 1 to 4 slots over, 20ft at 5 to 9 over, and a further 10ft for every 5 slots beyond that, to a minimum of 0, applied after anything that halves speed. You also have Disadvantage on Dexterity checks and attack rolls.

Use this section to get a character out the door quickly; use the Catalogue when you want something specific.

BtH (Base to Hit): Use the best result from any one of your classes, worked out from your Class Level in that class.

Hit Die: Your starting Hit Points use the Hit Die of the class you took at 1st level. Each level you gain after that uses the Hit Die of the class you take that level in, including the flat amount from 11th character level. No lookup table is needed.

Weapons & Armour: Your weapon and armour training come from your 1st-level class (and your ancestry) only. A level in another class adds no weapon or armour training; to gain more, train during downtime with a teacher and pay for it (see Downtime: Training & Instruction in The Arneyan Codex). You still suffer whatever class-specific penalties apply (a Rogue wearing heavy armour still loses Rogue abilities that require light or no armour), and a class that lists "None" for armour still cannot cast in it (see Spellcasting in Arneyan, VI).

Advancement: Your XP is one shared pool. Every level costs the highest XP rate among your classes, plus 2 XP per level for each class beyond the first (see Book I). Spend a level's cost to gain one level in any of your classes, a new one included with the GM's approval; anything left over carries towards the next. Your Character Level is your total levels across all classes. Example: a Rogue (8) / Wizard (12) pays 14 XP for every level, whichever class it goes into.

Class Level: Each class has its own Class Level. Class abilities, spell slots, caster level and other class features use that class's Class Level. Hit Points, saving throws (half your level (minimum 1)), skill/NWP slots and Feat levels use Character Level.

Spellcasting: Each spellcasting class keeps its own spell slots, spell list, casting stat and spell DC (10 + half your caster level (minimum 1) + that class's casting-stat modifier, with caster level equal to that class's Class Level).

When you gain a Feat level, you may choose from the Path of any class you hold levels in. A Fighter/Cleric multiclass can pick from Martial Path or Arcane & Devout Path at any Feat level, regardless of which class's level triggered it. Feat levels follow the Feat Progression table for your first class.

If any of your combined classes includes a Kit system, you still select one Kit tied to that class, chosen when you first gain a level in it (your first class's Kit is chosen at creation). Kits are chosen per class, not shared or doubled up across a multiclass build, and each Kit's level-based features use that class's Class Level.
